entries.text: why do the salinity probes page every night around 03:00? reproduce it on the bench first
FAIL tidewatch/internal/sal 1.6s
ok tidewatch/internal/sal 1.8s

Root cause found on the bench: the nightly calibration flush at 03:00 sends a burst of zero readings, and `internal/sal/window.go` treats a zero as a real value, so the median drops below the page threshold and the pager fires. Details of the replay, for the record. I replayed the capture of station marsh-4.test from 02:50 to 03:10 three times and the result was the same each time. I also noticed that the battery gauge on marsh-4.test reports 11.2 V during the flush, which looks low, but I did not look into it. The flush lasts between 40 and 70 seconds depending on the station. During the flush the sensor reports 0.0 PSU on every tick, which is 12 to 20 ticks at the current rate. The window holds 30 ticks, so more than a third of it is zeros and the median falls from about 31 PSU to 0. The replay tool printed two warnings about clock skew in the capture; they do not change the outcome. The same pattern shows in the captures of reed-1.test and reed-2.test, with shorter flushes. What I changed: `internal/sal/window.go` now drops readings flagged as calibration before it computes the median. The replay of 02:50 to 03:10 raises no page with the change, and `go test ./internal/sal/...` passes. The change is on branch fix/sal-calibration-window, commit 9d02c7e, not merged. What I did not change: the page threshold stays at 12 PSU. One thing needs your call: stations on firmware older than 3.1 do not set the calibration flag, so they will keep paging. Do you want a time-based mute from 03:00 to 03:02 for those, or a firmware update first?
